prompt: A call center wants to cut waiting times without hiring. Which takeaway matters most?

options.feedback: Right. Waits reach 12–14 minutes at 12pm and 1pm and stay at 6 minutes or less the rest of the day, so shifting staff into midday could fix it without hiring.

options.text: The average wait across the day is about 6 minutes
options.feedback: True, but the average hides the problem: waits reach 12–14 minutes at midday.

options.text: Waits build steadily through the day
options.feedback: Waits peak at 12–1pm and fall back to 2 minutes by 5pm.

options.text: Agents all take lunch at the same time
options.feedback: The chart shows waits by hour, not staff schedules. That may be true, but nothing here supports it.

explanation: Waits reach 12–14 minutes at 12pm and 1pm and stay at 6 minutes or less the rest of the day.

extras.proof: Waits reach 12–14 minutes at 12pm and 1pm and stay at 6 minutes or less the rest of the day.
